United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

title.narrative: Ratification of the 1970 Convention for the means of Prohibiting and Preventing the Illicit Import, Export and Transfer of Ownership of Cultural Property and strengthening policy for the return and restitution of cultural property in Namibia.

description.narrative:
Efforts to combat the illicit import, export, and transfer of ownership of cultural property need to be enhanced in Southern Africa, particularly through the implementation of the 1970 Convention on the Means of Prohibiting and Preventing the Illicit Import, Export, and Transfer of Ownership of Cultural Property. Namibia has yet to ratify the Convention. However, as part of the efforts towards securing Namibia's ratification, two workshops were organized at regional and national levels in 2021 and 2022. The national workshop held in 2022 moved a motion for Namibia to ratify the 1970 Convention. Following this, the Ministry of Education, Arts, and Culture was expected to initiate and lead the ratification process. Further to its ratification, efforts will be made to domesticate the Convention and develop guidelines on repatriation and inventorying of artifacts.
UNESCO will support the Ministry of Education, Arts, and Culture efforts in presenting the draft policy on human remains and artifacts for consultation to all 14 regions of Namibia, which is a required step for its completion. Additionally, guidelines on handling human remains and artifacts need to be drafted. UNESCO will also support this activity during the course of the biennium.
